title: North Carolina's 4th Congressional District election, 2026
description: North Carolina's 4th Congressional District, anchored by Durham, Chapel Hill, and Cary, is a reliably Democratic seat covering the Research Triangle region. Incumbent Representative Valerie Foushee, first elected in 2022, narrowly won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary against progressive challenger Nida Allam. She faces Republican Mahesh Ganorkar, an anti-socialism activist and small-business owner, and Libertarian Guy Meilleur, a consulting arborist, in the general election. The district was redrawn in October 2025 but remains strongly Democratic with a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+23. The race is rated 'Solid D' by the Cook Political Report, making Foushee the heavy favorite for re-election.
polling_note: No public general election polls for this race were found as of June 2026. The Cook Political Report rates this race as 'Solid D.'

candidates.name: Valerie Foushee
candidates.summary: Valerie Foushee is the Democratic incumbent representing North Carolina's 4th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. She previously served in the North Carolina State Senate (2013–2022), North Carolina State House (2012–2013), as chair of the Orange County Board of Commissioners (2004–2012), and on the Chapel Hill-Carrboro City Schools Board (1997–2004). She worked as an administrative officer for the Chapel Hill Police Department from 1987 to 2008. Foushee is the first African American and first woman to represent the 4th District in Congress. She earned a B.A. in Political Science and African and Afro-American Studies from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 2008.

candidates.name: Mahesh Ganorkar
candidates.summary: Mahesh 'Max' Ganorkar is the Republican nominee for North Carolina's 4th Congressional District. He holds an MBA in International Finance and has worked on international joint ventures and a family-owned construction business. Ganorkar describes himself as an 'anti-socialism warrior' and previously ran a TEA Party group to educate Americans about socialism. He has run for Congress previously in other North Carolina districts. He lives in Pittsboro with his wife of 33 years; they have three children. His campaign focuses on constitutional conservatism, limited government, and opposing socialism.

candidates.name: Guy Meilleur
candidates.summary: Guy Meilleur is the Libertarian Party nominee for North Carolina's 4th Congressional District. He is an ISA Board-Certified Master Arborist and consulting arborist who moved to Wake County in 1985 to study at North Carolina State University under renowned horticulturist J.C. Raulston. Meilleur previously ran unsuccessfully for North Carolina House District 30 in 2022 as a Libertarian. He lives in Durham and his campaign priorities include electoral reform, instant-runoff voting, restorative justice, cost-effective conservation, and expanding housing.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polls exist for this race, which limits direct measurement of voter preferences and keeps confidence at medium rather than high. However, the structural signals are overwhelmingly clear: North Carolina's 4th District has a Cook PVI of D+23, Cook Political Report rates the race 'Solid D,' and the seat covers the heavily Democratic Research Triangle (Durham, Chapel Hill, Cary). Incumbent Valerie Foushee (D) benefits from incumbency, a strong local political history, and a district that remained strongly Democratic after the October 2025 redistricting. The Republican nominee (Mahesh Ganorkar) and Libertarian nominee (Guy Meilleur) face an extremely uphill challenge in a D+23 district. Based on the available district fundamentals, Democrats are overwhelming favorites to retain this seat, consistent with the safe D rating (95%+ party win probability). The margin estimate of ~27 points reflects the D+23 baseline plus incumbency advantage.
